newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent clings to earlier gains in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent clings to earlier gains in nervous trade.

text.p: IPE oil futures clung to earlier gains in a nervous market following the opening of the NYMEX, with traders eyeing the direction of the New York market with trepidation.
"It's been a fairly quiet day," one trader said. "But we're at the mercy of the U.S. and the market's fairly nervous after the past week's falls."

May IPE Brent was trading six cents higher at $18.24 a barrel at 1518 GMT, having traded up as high as $18.36 and as low as $18.15 immediately after NYMEX's open. The May contract plunged as low as $18.07 on Thursday, a level not seen since June 25 last year.
"I don't know if we've hit the bottom yet," said one trader. "We have to wait and see what NYMEX does."
The next support for the May contract was pegged at $18 by a number of players.
April gas oil was 75 cents higher at $162.75 a tonne.
